args.rationale: Under AML Rulebook Chapter 14 (Rule 14.3.1), the internal suspicious-activity report to the MLRO must be made as soon as practicable and in any event within three (3) business days of the suspicion arising. The client identified the suspicious transaction on 3 August and filed its internal report on 10 August — the seventh business day after the suspicion arose (the task states the report was filed seven business days after the suspicion arose). This exceeds the three-business-day deadline, and MLRO leave does not excuse the delay. The withdrawn 2023 summary that stated a 10-business-day deadline was superseded and must not be relied upon. The client therefore breached the internal reporting deadline.
